author.name: Daniel Kahneman
author.heading: About Daniel Kahneman
author.bio: Daniel Kahneman (1934–2024) was an Israeli-American psychologist associated with Princeton University. His work with Amos Tversky helped explain systematic patterns in judgment and decision-making; he received the 2002 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences and brought this research to a broad readership in Thinking, Fast and Slow.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The cited sentence appears in the book’s discussion of evaluating life and happiness. It warns that the subject occupying attention can temporarily dominate judgment. Read in that setting, it concerns distorted weighting rather than the assertion that nothing in life matters.
